profile.campus: Digital Realty Chicago (downtown / Elk Grove Village / Franklin Park), IL
profile.reading:
This is Digital Realty facility ORD11, at 600 South Federal Street, Chicago, IL 60605. Digital Realty's own property listing for ORD11, fetched this session, lists the building at 146,000 square feet.

Digital Realty Trust (NYSE: DLR, SEC CIK 1297996), headquartered at 2323 Bryan Street, Dallas, Texas, reported 310 data centers worldwide as of December 31, 2025, 221 wholly owned or consolidated and 89 in unconsolidated joint ventures, about 57.6 million rentable square feet across more than 55 metro markets including 118 US facilities, per its FY2025 Form 10-K filed with the SEC. The company operates as a colocation and wholesale landlord rather than running its own compute, distinguishing it from hyperscaler tenants such as AWS, Google, or Meta, also tracked in this registry.

This building is part of Digital Realty's Chicago metro footprint, anchored by the much larger Lakeside Technology Center at 350 East Cermak Road and including a cluster of suburban buildings in Elk Grove Village and Franklin Park near O'Hare International Airport. Digital Realty markets its Chicago properties under its PlatformDIGITAL brand, positioning the metro alongside Northern Virginia, Dallas, Silicon Valley, and New York/New Jersey, all tracked elsewhere in this registry, as core hubs in its global interconnection and colocation platform. The company does not publish a consolidated IT power rating in megawatts for individual Chicago buildings in the sources reviewed this session.

Digital Realty's FY2025 Form 10-K identifies the United States as its largest single national market by both facility count and rentable square footage. Illinois has offered data center-specific state tax incentives, administered by the Illinois Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity, that local officials have credited with helping draw large colocation and hyperscale investment to the Chicago metro.

reading.body:
Digital Realty ORD11 is a 146,000 square foot colocation building at 600 South Federal Street in downtown Chicago, part of Digital Reality's multi-property Chicago metro portfolio anchored by the much larger Lakeside Technology Center. The operator does not publish an IT megawatt capacity figure for this specific building in its property page or in its FY2025 10-K filing with the SEC, so the IT load available to tenants cannot be stated from disclosed specifications.

ORD11 is one of 44 mapped data center facilities in Illinois and one of six whose operators have published power capacity ratings; across those six, Illinois hosts 236 megawatts of disclosed IT load. This building ranks seventh by published megawatt capacity within the state, though that ranking reflects only the six facilities with disclosed figures and does not include this one. Chicago's principal utility is ComEd. Illinois offers data center-specific state tax incentives through the Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity that local officials credit with attracting large colocation and hyperscale operators to the metro.

Digital Realty operates as a colocation and wholesale landlord, renting space and power to tenants rather than running compute itself. The company reported 310 data centers worldwide as of December 31, 2025, with 118 US facilities across more than 55 metro markets. Without a published megawatt figure for ORD11, this building's relevance to AI scaling depends on the power density and utilization of its current or future tenants, which are not published here.
